name: Sales forecast
summary: A weekly sales forecast for a team: each salesperson's commit, best case, closed this quarter and pipeline, the team's figures added up, the gap to quota and pipeline coverage worked out, a dashboard and a deck for the weekly meeting and a Workflow that asks on Monday and has the sales lead approve.

whatItsFor.text: For a sales team that calls its quarter every week. On Monday each salesperson's figures for the week just ended come in, the sales lead approves them, and the team reads its **commit**, gap to quota and pipeline coverage.
For the weekly forecast meeting it brings:

items: Figures for each salesperson, and the team's figures added up from them.
A **dashboard** with this week's call against quota, each salesperson's commit against theirs and the last 13 weeks.
A **deck** of seven slides that fills in its own figures, with the gap by salesperson.
A **Workflow** that asks, has each value approved, locks the week and sends its Snapshot.
n8n templates that send figures from HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel.
An **Owner** installs the Pack, because it holds three Themes. An Owner or Admin sets it up.
Your salespeople, up to 30. Invite them on the **Members** page, or add them as Contacts, so that you can pick them.
A **sales lead**, a member of the Workspace, who approves the figures. Nobody approves their own value while someone else can.
Each salesperson's **quota** for the quarter. You set it once, as the target of their **Commit**. The team's quota is those added up.
Where **Closed this quarter** and **Pipeline value** come from: your CRM or a sheet through n8n, or people who type them.
Room in your Workspace's size: **4 Metrics** for each salesperson and **8** for the team. Ten salespeople make 48.
The money figures are in euro. If yours differ, change the **Unit** with **Edit details…** on each Metric's **Description** tab.

firstSteps.text: Do these in order. After that the week runs by itself.

items: Open **Settings**, then **Packs**. Under this Pack, choose **Set up from this Pack**.
Under **List each Salesperson**, add a line for each one: type their name and answer **Who is the Salesperson?** Under **Who does what**, answer **Who is the Sales lead?**
Keep the Metrics ticked, with the dashboard **Weekly forecast meeting** and the Workflow **Weekly sales forecast**.
Under **Shares the Pack proposes**, choose **Tick all for** the sales lead: a team figure is shown only to someone who sees every salesperson's figure it adds up.
Choose **Set up**. No request goes out unless you tick **Send the first requests now**; otherwise people are asked at the Workflow's next run.

Set the quotas: open each salesperson's **Commit**, go to the **Targets** tab and give every week of the quarter their quarter's quota. **Paste from a spreadsheet** takes the weeks in one go. For a team quota of its own, see **Questions**.
To connect a CRM or a sheet, choose **Fill from n8n** on the page Set up shows. In n8n, leave the settings for the team's figures empty and give each salesperson a line in the node **Owners**.
Send this week's figures: whoever submits answers the request, or opens the Metric and chooses **Record a value**. The sales lead then approves them.
Open **Decks**, choose **From a Deck Template**, pick **Weekly forecast meeting** and a Metric for each Slot. Each Slot is named like the Metric it takes.
On Monday Ziffr asks the people who send figures for the week just ended, and the n8n templates send theirs. The figures are due on Tuesday, with a reminder that day.
The sales lead approves each value. It is then published and the week is locked.
Before the meeting, open the deck and write what only you know over the questions on its slides, such as why the pipeline moved and what you ask for.
Once the week is finished, the sales lead gets a link to its Snapshot. Add others in the Workflow's **Send Snapshot** step and share the dashboard with them.
When a new quarter starts, add its weeks and quotas on each **Commit**'s **Targets** tab.
Someone joins: under this Pack choose **Add a Salesperson**, tick the team figures that count the new one, then set their quota.
Someone leaves: archive their Metrics. Ziffr asks up to which week each team figure counts them, and earlier weeks stay.
**Commit**: what they commit to closing by the end of the quarter, deals already won included. Its target is their quota.
**Best case**: what the quarter reaches if the open deals that may still close do, deals already won included.
**Closed this quarter**: the value of the deals won since the quarter began. It starts again from 0 each quarter.
**Pipeline value**: all open deals that can still close this quarter, those in the commit included, those already won not.
**Team commit**, **Team best case**, **Team closed this quarter** and **Team pipeline value**: Totals that add up the figures of all salespeople. Nobody sends them.
**Quota**: the salespeople's quotas added up.
**Commit gap to quota**: Team commit minus the quota. Below 0, the commit is that much short.
**Commit as share of quota**: Team commit as a percentage of the quota. 100 % or more covers it.
**Pipeline coverage**: Team pipeline value divided by what is still missing, which is the quota minus Team closed this quarter.
The dashboard **Weekly forecast meeting**: the call against quota, the change on last week, the last 13 weeks and each salesperson's commit against their quota.
The deck **Weekly forecast meeting**: a cover, the call, where the gap sits by salesperson, the change since last week, the weeks of the quarter, pipeline coverage, and the risks and asks.

The Workflow **Weekly sales forecast**: asks on Monday, reminds on Tuesday, tells the Metric's owner about a missing value on Wednesday, marks a change of more than 25 % as unusual, has every value approved, locks the week and sends its Snapshot.
**Forecast Navy**, **Forecast Coral** and **Forecast Forest**: three Themes. The deck starts with Navy. Add your logo to the Theme you use under **Themes** in **Settings**.

questions.text: Who sees what?

Each salesperson sees their own figures. The sales lead sees everyone's once the proposed Shares are ticked. A team figure is shown only to someone who sees every salesperson's figure it adds up; the Metric's owner can show a team figure to others on its page.
Why is a team figure empty?

It has a value for a week once every salesperson's figure is in: someone with nothing sends 0. The quota, and what follows from it, also needs a target on every salesperson's **Commit** for that week.
How do we give the team a quota of its own?
To begin with, the team's quota is the salespeople's quotas added up. For another one, such as a quota with a margin on top, the owner or an Editor of **Team commit** does this:

items: Open **Metrics**, then **Team commit**. On the **Overview** tab, find **What it adds up**.
Under **Target**, choose **Its own target**. Ziffr says **Target changed**.
Open the **Targets** tab. Choose **Add row** for each week, or **Paste from a spreadsheet** with two columns: the week and the quota.
Give every week of the quarter the team's quota for the quarter, also past weeks you still want to read. Then press the **Save** button below the rows.

questions.text: **Quota**, **Commit gap to quota**, **Commit as share of quota** and **Pipeline coverage** then use the team's own quota, on the dashboard and on the slides. A week without one has none of these, past weeks too.
The slide with the gap by salesperson stays as it was: each row compares a salesperson with their own quota. So the rows need not add up to the team's gap.
For one quota that holds in every week, choose **Edit details…** on the **Description** tab and fill in **Target from**. It keeps no history: changing it changes past weeks too.
While **Team commit** is shown to people who do not see every salesperson's figure, only its owner changes the target, and ticks the box that asks them to confirm.
How do we go back to the quotas added up?

items: Open **Team commit**, and on the **Overview** tab under **Target** choose **Its Metrics’ targets added up**.
Check that each salesperson's **Commit** has a target for the weeks you read: a week has a team quota only when every one of them has one.

questions.text: This removes a **Target from** or **Target up to** set on **Team commit**. The weekly quotas you entered for it are kept but not used, and count again if you choose **Its own target** later.
Can the figures come from our CRM?

Yes. n8n can send **Closed this quarter** and **Pipeline value** for each salesperson every Monday from HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive. HubSpot and Salesforce can also send **Commit** and **Best case** if you switch them on; Commit is otherwise a person's call. n8n runs on your side, and Ziffr never holds your CRM login.
Can they come from a spreadsheet, or can we type them?

Both. **Fill from n8n** also offers Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel templates, and any figure of a salesperson can be typed by whoever submits it. Figures of earlier weeks can be brought in with **Paste values**.
Which week does a figure belong to?

Each week holds the figures as they stood at its end. A reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended. In a week that spans two quarters, send the figures of the quarter the week starts in.
We set the Pack up before version 2
What was set up stays as it is and keeps working. To change to figures for each salesperson, update the Pack and set it up again.
Is this the same as the Sales Pack?
No. The Sales Pack counts a month's leads and deals. Sales forecast is a Pack of its own, and you can have both.

metric.name: Commit
metric.description: One salesperson's forecast call: what they commit to closing by the end of the quarter, deals already won in it included. Its target is their quota: set it on the Targets tab for each week of the quarter. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered.
metric.calculationNote: The value of the deals this salesperson has won this quarter plus the open deals they commit to closing by its end, as it stands at the end of the week. Deals that count only in the best case, and deals expected after the quarter, are left out.

metric.name: Best case
metric.description: What one salesperson's quarter reaches if the open deals that may still close do: commit plus upside, deals already won included. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered.
metric.calculationNote: The salesperson's commit plus the upside: the further open deals that may still close by the end of the quarter, as they stand at the end of the week. Deals already lost and deals expected after the quarter are left out.

metric.name: Closed this quarter
metric.description: The value of the deals one salesperson has won since the quarter began. It starts again from 0 each quarter; a week that spans two quarters belongs to the one it starts in. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered.
metric.calculationNote: The value of every deal the salesperson has won from the first day of the quarter to the end of the week, added up. Open deals are not in it, and it starts again from 0 with the next quarter.

metric.name: Pipeline value
metric.description: The value of one salesperson's open deals that can still close this quarter, those in the commit included, those already won not. Taken as it stood at the end of the week: a reply to Monday's request counts for the week just ended, and so does its form link while the request is unanswered.
metric.calculationNote: The full value of every deal of the salesperson still open at the end of the week that can close this quarter, not weighted by its chance. Committed deals that are still open are in it; deals already won and deals expected after the quarter are not.

metric.name: Team commit
metric.description: The commit of every salesperson, added up. A week has a sum once each Commit is in; a salesperson with nothing sends 0. Its target, the team's quota, is their targets added up.
metric.calculationNote: Commit of every salesperson for the week, added up. There is no sum while one of them is missing, and no target while one of them has none.

metric.name: Team best case
metric.description: The best case of every salesperson, added up. A week has a sum once each is in.
metric.calculationNote: Best case of every salesperson for the week, added up. There is no sum while one of them is missing.

metric.name: Team closed this quarter
metric.description: What every salesperson has won since the quarter began, added up. A week has a sum once each is in.
metric.calculationNote: Closed this quarter of every salesperson for the week, added up. There is no sum while one of them is missing.

metric.name: Team pipeline value
metric.description: The open deals of every salesperson that can still close this quarter, added up. A week has a sum once each is in.
metric.calculationNote: Pipeline value of every salesperson for the week, added up. There is no sum while one of them is missing.

metric.name: Quota
metric.description: The team's quota for the quarter, read from the target of Team commit, so nobody sends it. That target is the salespeople's quotas added up: set each on the Targets tab of their Commit. Empty in a week without a Team commit.
metric.calculationNote: The target of Team commit for the week: the targets of every salesperson's Commit added up. There is no value in a week without a Team commit or while a salesperson has no target.

metric.name: Commit gap to quota
metric.description: Team commit minus the quota for the week. Below 0, the commit is that much short; 0 or more covers it. Empty until the week has a Team commit and a quota.
metric.calculationNote: Team commit less its target, which holds the quota, both of the same week. A figure below 0 is what the commit lacks to reach the quota, and there is no value in a week without a Team commit or a quota.

metric.name: Commit as share of quota
metric.description: Team commit as a share of the quota for the same week. 100 % or more covers it. Empty until the week has a Team commit and a quota, and when the quota is 0.
metric.calculationNote: Team commit divided by its target, which holds the quota, in percent, both of the same week. There is no value in a week without a Team commit or a quota, or when the quota is 0.

metric.name: Pipeline coverage
metric.description: Team pipeline value divided by what is still missing, which is the quota minus Team closed this quarter. 3 times means the open deals are worth three times what is missing. Empty when a figure or the quota is missing or exactly nothing is left to close. Below 0 when more than the quota is closed: then nothing is left to cover.
metric.calculationNote: Team pipeline value divided by the target of Team commit less Team closed this quarter, all of the same week: how many times the open deals cover what is still to be closed. There is no value when a figure or the quota is missing or exactly nothing is left to close, and a value below 0 means that more than the quota is already closed.

template.name: Weekly sales forecast
template.description: Asks each salesperson on Monday for the week just ended, due Tuesday with a reminder, then tells the Metric Owner. The sales lead approves every value, which publishes and locks. Once the week is finished it sends the dashboard's Snapshot to the sales lead.
